protocol: D-000 new cycle, turn 1 of 3; refute not confirm; records section31-supplier-coverage.v4 and checker v4 as the Lane R successor to D-043's v3
summary: Every named attack fails and I found nothing to add. All six cited digests match live bytes, including my own v4 verdict at 7bef5029 characterized exactly as ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES 0 blockers. The discharge split is correct in both directions: S31V3-01, S31V3-02 and S31V3-CX-A1 are discharged, which matches what I verified by execution on those bytes, and all four new advisories including both of mine are named as still owed. Clause 4 is byte-identical to D-043's adopted clause 4, carrying the full condition block, the MF-6 citation and D-038's forward-warning with nothing dropped. I verified Codex's S31V4-CX-A2 independently without reading its file, by running four adjacent malformed supplier shapes against the checker -- all four raise untyped exceptions, so the entry's characterization of that advisory is accurate. The register cites neither instrument version, so 'D-043 remains history' creates no conflicting live citation, which I checked rather than assumed.
whatIVerified: Subject digest at start and end: 915ecd4ccfa09497313748d387e8fc882bb0a5d2c1f5c237f5f5f9635d3719a4 both times, matching the dispatch's expected digest. No drift.

The attack 'cited digests do not match live bytes' fails on all six: instrument v4 97727684…, checker v4 a3092826…, Claude 2 7bef5029…, Codex 1db18b81…, COORD 3aec906f…, file 08 80fc55d1…. Each measured by me against live bytes. The file-08 and COORD pins are the current post-D-044 values, not carried-forward stale ones.

The attack 'cited verdicts were not 0-blocker ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES' fails on my half, from my own bytes: my v4 verdict carries verdict ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES, mustFix 0, shouldFix 2, and objection ids S31V4-01 and S31V4-02. The entry's characterization is exact.

The attack 'treats S31V3-* as still owed' fails and its converse holds. Clause 1 states S31V3-01, S31V3-02 and S31V3-CX-A1 are 'discharged by execution on these bytes', which matches my v4 review: I recorded all three REPAIRED, and proved S31V3-01 side by side by running the identical mutation against the v3 and v4 checkers -- KeyError under v3, typed 'FAIL - S31-1: BOUND item has no supplier' under v4.

The attack 'treats S31V4-01 / S31V4-02 / S31V4-CX-A1 / S31V4-CX-A2 as discharged' fails. Clause 3 names all four and closes 'Those advisories remain owed on a successor.' My two are described accurately and compressed without distortion: 'stale recordedInputs on COORD and file 08' is my S31V4-01, and 'whole-file freeze gate after D-044 gave DR-004 a §3.1 segment pin' is my S31V4-02, including the D-044 causation I established.

I verified Codex's S31V4-CX-A2 independently rather than accepting the entry's word or reading Codex's file. I ran four adjacent malformed supplier shapes against checker v4 on a scratchpad copy: a supplier dict with no path key gives KeyError: 'path'; a supplier that is a string gives TypeError: string indices must be integers; a null supplier gives TypeError: 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable; an item with no standing key gives KeyError: 'standing'. All four are untyped. 'Adjacent malformed supplier shapes still untyped' is an accurate description of the bytes.

Clause 4 is byte-identical to D-043's adopted clause 4. I extracted both and token-diffed them in each direction: nothing in D-043's clause 4 is absent from D-045's, and nothing is added. The full block travels intact -- rows stay HARD-BLOCKED, condition 1 does not discharge, DR-004's Route A still needs the eight-bullet Phase-1A packet with this instrument named as the other commissioned limb, conditions 2-5 remain, condition 5 remains the only implementation authorization, 'Does not edit file 08 (MF-6)', and D-038's forward-warning about a later file-08 cell note.

The attack 'silent SATISFIED, Phase-1A insertion, or condition-1 discharge' fails on all three. SATISFIED occurs once, in the refusal 'It is not SATISFIED evidence.' Phase-1A occurs twice, in 'It is not the Phase-1A packet' and the rejected alternative 'Treat the instrument as Phase-1A insertion. Rejected.' Condition-1 discharge is expressly denied in clause 4.

The attack 'treats bound=1 / unbound=7 as complete coverage' fails. Clause 2 states the counts, and clause 3 opens the unmet list with 'the seven UNBOUND items' -- the small count is treated as the finding rather than the result.

The attack 'treats item 1 as BOUND' fails. Clause 2: 'Item 1 stays UNBOUND because no head supplies verdict claims together with match / no-match / indeterminate / error', which is my original four-category argument and matches v4's own UNBOUND reason.

The attacks 'file-08 edited without MF-6' and 'freeze / blueprint motion' both fail. Clause 4 carries the MF-6 citation and forward-warning, and states no freeze motion and no blueprint. git reports file 08, the freeze, the blueprint, COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md and the claim matrix all unmodified, so nothing has been pre-applied ahead of this entry's adoption.

'D-043 remains history' creates no conflicting live citation, which I checked at the bytes rather than assuming. File 08 does not cite the instrument at any version -- zero occurrences of section31-supplier-coverage.v3 and zero of v4 -- so there is no register cell left pointing at the superseded generation and no MF-6 edit owed to fix one.

The form claim 'Same form as D-035 / D-038 / D-042 / D-043' is accurate and all four precedents are adopted: D-042 at 4e23a2e, D-043 at a5d3719, with D-035 and D-038 adopted earlier. D-043's adopted entry confirms the same recording shape, including its own Subject and Verdicts lines carrying both file digests.

The D-001 commission link survives the change in clause 1's framing. D-043 clause 1 read 'D-001 commissioned and D-036 started on Lane R'; D-045 clause 1 reads 'succeeding D-043's v3'. The commission is not lost -- clause 4 still names this instrument as 'the other commissioned limb' of DR-004's Route A. Examined and declined as a finding.

The entry handles the awkward case correctly rather than hiding it. It pins file 08 at the live post-D-044 value while recording an instrument whose own recordedInputs pin file 08 at the superseded 877e36d3, and it discloses exactly that gap in clause 3 as S31V4-01. That is the right disposition, and it is the opposite of the defect I raised against permission-truth-tables.v2, where a refreshed environment pin sat beside an unrefreshed carried row with nothing saying so.

The entry is single-subject and severable: 'section31-supplier-coverage.v4.json and its checker check-section31-supplier-coverage-v4.py only.' Recording table and checker together is right here, since the checker is half of what my v4 review measured and S31V3-01 was a defect in the checker rather than the table.

Examined and declined: clause 1 says all three predecessor findings are 'discharged by execution on these bytes', though S31V3-02 is a disclosure added to doesNotFailWhen rather than a code path that can be run. I decline it because the dispatch for v4 framed all three as 'repairs to verify by execution, not trust', and my own v4 verdict recorded all three under a section headed namedRepairsVerifiedByExecution -- I did verify S31V3-02's claim against the code by confirming resolve() tests key presence only, which is execution-grounded even though the repair itself is text. If that phrasing overstates, I overstated first, and it would be inconsistent to object to the entry adopting my own characterization.

reviewerSelfCorrection.what: Verifying S31V4-CX-A2 showed my own S31V3-01 was narrower than the defect class it belonged to. I flagged that a BOUND item with no supplier key raised KeyError, and the v4 repair guards exactly that one case. Four adjacent shapes in the same loop -- supplier without path, supplier as a string, supplier as null, item without standing -- still raise untyped exceptions.
reviewerSelfCorrection.pattern: Reporting the instance I tripped over instead of asking what else in the same function is unguarded. It is the same family as the misses I have already recorded in this protocol: checking the thing pointed at rather than the class it belongs to. Here it cost nothing, because Codex caught the generalization and D-045 carries it as an owed advisory, but a narrower fix landed than the code needed.
reviewerSelfCorrection.correctionApplied: When a finding is 'this input crashes rather than failing typed', enumerate the sibling inputs in the same code path before writing it up. I did that here for S31V4-CX-A2's verification and found all four, which is how I could confirm the advisory without reading Codex's file.

whatIDidNotCheck: The Codex review of D-045. Not read; the file is confirmed absent at review time.

The Codex v4 verdict, and its ids S31V4-CX-A1 and S31V4-CX-A2 as Codex states them. I verified the digest 1db18b81… and I verified the SUBSTANCE both advisories describe -- the stale COORD and file-08 pins, and the four untyped malformed shapes -- against the bytes myself. I did not verify that Codex's verdict class is ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES, that its blocker count is zero, or that its finding ids are the ones recited. If that characterization is wrong, clause 1's '0 blockers from both reviewers' premise and the D-035 gate both fail, and nothing in my review would detect it.

Whether any of the seven UNBOUND items could now be bound. I verified in the v4 review that S31-1's and S31-4's reasons are true at the bytes; I did not sweep the corpus for candidate suppliers for the rest.

The merits of section31-supplier-coverage.v4 and checker v4 beyond my separate review at 7bef5029, whose stated limits I carry forward: I did not test resolve() on selector forms the single bound row does not exercise, and I did not judge whether product-dispositions.v1's CD-RT-5 is itself sound.

Whether v3's checker remaining on disk and still passing creates any practical ambiguity about which check is operative. I examined it and concluded clause 1's succession statement settles it -- v4 succeeds v3, so v4's checker is the accepted one -- and that running a superseded checker is a user error rather than a defect in this entry. I did not pursue it further.
Whether the DR-004 and DR-002 owners will act on this recording. It binds nothing and changes neither row's standing.

environment.gitHeadSubject: D-044: perform the D-033 property-pin rewrite
environment.note: The subject and review prompt are untracked working-tree files at review time; digests bind working-tree bytes, not committed objects. Recorded as a condition of review, not a finding, since the draft is pre-adoption and binds nothing.
environment.measurementTool: shasum -a 256; awk extraction of adopted D-043 and its clause 4 with a two-directional token diff against D-045's clause 4; grep of file 08 for instrument citations at any version; a four-case executable probe of adjacent malformed supplier shapes against checker v4 on a scratchpad copy, to verify Codex's S31V4-CX-A2 without reading Codex's file; git status across file 08, freeze, blueprint, COORD and the claim matrix

consentNote: I CONSENT at turn 1 with zero findings, which I have not done often in this series, so I state what I attacked. I did not accept the entry's account of either reviewer: I measured all six digests, confirmed my own verdict's class and counts from my file, and verified the substance of the one Codex advisory I could test by running four malformed shapes through the checker myself. I did not accept that clause 4 matched its precedent: I extracted D-043's adopted clause 4 and token-diffed it both ways against this one. I did not accept that 'D-043 remains history' was safe: I checked whether the register cites either instrument version, and it cites neither. The discharge split is the part that could most easily have gone wrong -- three predecessor findings closed, four new ones kept open -- and it is exactly right in both directions.
